name: Garden
notes: USDA Zone 7a, Middle Tennessee. Avg last spring frost ~Apr 12-15; avg first fall frost ~Oct 23. Garden year runs Sep 1 - Aug 31. 6 rotating sections (S1/S2/S3 on the South Bed; N1/N2/N3 on the North Bed) cycling 6 groups on a 6-year return: Legumes->Brassicas, Solanaceae, Cucurbits, Roots & chenopods, Alliums (garlic+onion), Strawberries. Peppers, fall carrots, fall tomatoes, mint live in the pot annex on fresh media. Herbs at the patio. Plan is date-driven via UT back-count method, so most triggers are calendar (not condition) by design. Activities dated 2026-07 through 2027-01 are the near-term first-cycle build from '2026 fall step-by-step'; activities dated 2027-02 onward are the recurring standing annual backbone from succession-system-v4 (advance one section per January). Four introduction-control rules override everything: certified strawberry plugs, certified seed garlic, BLS-screened pepper seed, home-grown brassica starts.

activities.name: Order Fall & Winter Supplies
activities.description: Order the full fall/winter input list in one pass. Certified seed garlic sells out by late summer. ORDER LIST: (1) Certified seed garlic 2 lb hardneck+softneck, (2) Cowpea inoculant, (3) Pinkeye Purple Hull pea seed 72 ct, (4) Watermelon radish (Beauty Heart) + Hakurei turnip seed for N1, (5) Mache/corn salad seed (Vit) for N3, (6) Spinach (Bloomsdale Long Standing) + romaine lettuce seed for S3 gap filler.

steps.name: Certified seed garlic (2 lb, hardneck+softneck)
steps.description: Music or German Extra Hardy (hardneck), Inchelium Red (softneck). Never grocery-store garlic (white rot).

steps.name: Cowpea inoculant (Bradyrhizobium, cowpea/peanut group)
steps.description: NOT the bean or garden-pea type. ~$6.

steps.name: Pinkeye Purple Hull pea seed (bush type)
Watermelon radish (Beauty Heart) + Hakurei turnip seed
steps.description: For N1 in September. Both direct-sow, cold-tolerant.

steps.name: Mache / corn salad seed (Vit)
Spinach (Bloomsdale Long Standing) + romaine lettuce seed
steps.description: For S3 gap filler after tomato pull.

activities.name: Sow Cabbage Indoors
activities.description: 7 seeds (+ spares): 3 Flat Dutch (24 in spacing, 85 DTM) and 4 Red Acre (18 in spacing, 75 DTM) for the N2 fall brassica planting. Miss the July sow and there is no fall crop.

steps.name: Prepare cells with clean seed-starting mix
Sow 1/4 in deep, germinate at 75F
Move seedlings to 60-65F under light after emergence
steps.description: 78F house makes leggy brassicas. Garage/basement shop light is ideal.

activities.name: Plant Southern Peas in S2
activities.description: S2 is bare on a slope in July. Pinkeye Purple Hull, 72 seeds, opening the Legumes->Brassicas leg.

steps.name: Rake bed level, add NO nitrogen/compost
steps.description: Excess N gives vines and no pods.

steps.name: Inoculate seed in shade, plant within an hour
steps.description: UV and heat kill the rhizobia.

steps.name: Sow 2 rows 20 in apart, 4 in in-row, 1.5 in deep, dry
Water in thoroughly at planting
Check germination (5-7 days)

activities.name: Cut Potato Tops (S1 & N1)
activities.description: Cut foliage at soil level on both towers to set skins. Do not pull.

steps.name: Cut foliage at soil level, leave tubers in media

activities.name: Dig Potatoes & Dismantle Towers
activities.description: Dig tubers after skins set, then clear both tower footprints in S1 and N1.

steps.name: Slice one tuber - check for internal heat necrosis
steps.description: Brown flecking near vascular ring = heat necrosis. Note for future container-potato decisions.

steps.name: Dump tower media to compost or lawn, NOT beds
Dismantle structures, clear S1 and N1 footprints

activities.name: Direct-Seed Collards in N2
activities.description: 8 seeds, 18 in spacing in row 2 (beside cabbage row). Direct-seed by Aug 14 (back-count: DTM 60 + 10 = 70 d from Oct 23). Collards handle direct seeding and late-summer heat. No indoor start needed.

steps.name: Sow 1/4 in deep in clean mix, then move to 60-65F

activities.name: Check / Renovate Strawberries in S1
activities.description: June-bearers should be done by mid-July. Renovate if done; let everbearing/day-neutral run to frost. This planting carries the 2027 Strawberry group.

steps.name: If June-bearing: mow to 1 in above crowns, thin runners to 4-6 in, light feed
If everbearing/day-neutral: skip renovation, harvest to frost

activities.name: Pull Tomatoes from S3 & N3 + Verticillium Check
activities.description: Pull when flower production stops. The stem-slice is the only real evidence of Verticillium you'll ever get.

steps.name: Slice each main stem near base - log vascular browning
steps.description: Slice each main stem near base - log vascular browning. DONE Aug 15 2026: All tomato stems checked, no vascular browning — Verticillium clear.

steps.name: Remove & bag ALL Solanaceae debris (leaves, fruit, root stubs)
Hold jalapeños in place; move to pots ~Sept 15
steps.description: Jalapeños still producing well in S3/N3 — leaving in place. Relocate best 2-3 to 5-gal pots near patio closer to Sept 15 (when fall planting goes into these beds). Pull the rest at that same time.

activities.name: Transplant Fall Brassicas into N2
activities.description: Row 1: 3 Flat Dutch (24 in) + 4 Red Acre (18 in) = 7 cabbage across 12 ft. Row 2: 8 collards already direct-seeded. Harvest Nov-Dec, sweeter after frost.

steps.name: Harden off seedlings 5-7 days (shade -> sun)
Water in deeply, mulch 2-3 in
steps.description: Mulch the entire 4 ft bed width — both rows AND the center band between them — with 2-3 in straw. Clean bare soil in September grows pigweed and crabgrass fast; the center band needs covering too. Leave a small collar cleared around each cabbage transplant, then let the brassicas canopy over by late October.

activities.name: Clear N1 as Pattypan Finishes
activities.description: Let squash produce until vine borer/mildew finishes it. Do NOT plant a second round - the open section is worth more. Pull and clear debris.

activities.name: Harvest Southern Peas in S2
activities.description: Pods turn purple at green-shell stage. Pick over 1-2 weeks; ~10 lb from 72 plants.

steps.name: Freeze surplus: shell, blanch 2 min, ice bath, freeze flat, bag

activities.name: Sow Watermelon Radish + Hakurei Turnips in N1
activities.description: Direct-sow watermelon radish (Beauty Heart) and hakurei turnips in N1 after summer cucurbits clear. Watermelon radish: 60 DTM, 4-inch spacing, 0.5-inch deep. Hakurei turnips: 38 DTM, 4-inch spacing, 0.5-inch deep. Both cold-tolerant, harvest before hard freeze.

steps.name: Thin to 1 per station at 2 in tall

activities.name: Sow Mache & Arugula in N3
activities.description: Sow mache + arugula as winter filler. Valerianaceae (mache) has no rotation conflict; arugula (Brassicaceae) is safe as baby green harvest with 3.5+ yr gap to next brassica year.

steps.name: Water gently; don't give up on it for weeks

activities.name: Cut Pea Vines in S2
activities.description: Cut at soil level. Do NOT pull - the fixed nitrogen is in the root nodules. Leave roots to decompose. 14 days before garlic.

steps.name: Chop tops into surface or remove to compost

activities.name: Garlic In - S2 (rows 1 & 3)
activities.description: The most important fall planting. 48 cloves across rows 1 & 3 of the full 12 ft section. 6 in in-row, 10 in between rows, 2 in deep, pointy end up. Onion transplants go into rows 2 & 4 in Feb. Straw mulch all garlic rows in November.

steps.name: Confirm certified seed garlic on hand
Separate cloves; plant the biggest, eat the small
Do NOT fertilize (pea roots decomposing underneath)

activities.name: Soil Test All Beds
activities.description: Test every vegetable bed plus blueberry site and patio herb site. pH moves take months, so October results drive spring amendments.

steps.name: Confirm vegetable beds stay above pH 7 (clubroot suppression)
Blueberry site wants 4.5-5.5 - plan sulfur now

activities.name: Pull Remaining Solanaceae / Jalapeno Pots
activities.description: After first frost (~Oct 23) or when they quit, pull potted jalapenos, dump media, clean pots for 2027.

steps.name: If growing peri peri: bring in at frost, cut back hard, overwinter by a window
steps.description: Year two fruits weeks earlier and much heavier.

activities.name: Sow Spinach on S2 Onion Half [SKIPPED]
activities.description: SKIPPED: garlic and onions now interplant in alternating rows across the full section. No separate onion half; no winter cover crop needed.

steps.name: Broadcast cereal rye on east half, rake in 1/4 in
Mulch garlic half 2-3 in straw (not hay, not leaves)

activities.name: Harvest Fall Brassicas from N2
activities.description: Cabbage: harvest when heads are firm and full-sized (Flat Dutch gets large, 10-15 in). Collards: outer leaves progressively. Both sweeter after frost.

steps.name: When finished, chop residue into soil (biofumigant into 2027 Solanaceae bed)

activities.name: Harvest Watermelon Radish + Hakurei Turnips from N1
activities.description: Hakurei turnips ready ~5 weeks after sowing (late Oct). Watermelon radish ready ~60 days after sowing (mid-Nov). Pull hakurei first, then watermelon radish. Clear bed before hard ground freeze for winter fallow.

activities.name: Remove Plum/Peach Tree (dormant)
activities.description: Take it out cleanly while dormant, or move it in-ground elsewhere. Do NOT pot it - a potted stone fruit in 7a freezes the root zone.

activities.name: Merge Beds 2 & 3 into 36 ft North Bed
activities.description: Target: 6 ft gap gives 36 ft = 3 x 12 ft sections matching Bed 1. Fill gap with 21 cu ft of 40/50/10 mix (8.4 topsoil / 10.5 compost / 2.1 sand).

steps.name: Measure the gap FIRST (4 ft leaves an awkward 34 ft)
Source ~1 pickup load of 40/50/10 fill

activities.name: Build Blueberry Bed
activities.description: Mix 50-80% aged pine bark fines / 10-40% sphagnum peat / 10% perlite. NOT the 40/50/10 mix. Keep 4+ ft off the foundation.

steps.name: Order bark fines / peat / perlite
Install rain barrel on nearest downspout
steps.description: 193 mg/L irrigation water pushes bed pH up; rainwater solves it.

activities.name: Move Blueberries (dormant)
activities.description: Dig with a generous root ball, plant at same depth, water in, mulch 3-4 in pine bark. No fertilizer until spring growth.

activities.name: Cut Root Barrier Trenches at Both Apples
activities.description: 12-18 in vertical trench at each drip line (S1, N1), lined with 60-mil pond liner / HDPE / scrap roofing, backfilled. Makes S1/N1 real rotating sections. Re-cut every 2-3 years.

activities.name: Prune Overhanging Limbs on Berry Beds (dormant)
activities.description: Dormant pruning. If any are oaks, dormant timing is essential (oak wilt). Then measure actual sun hours before any cane decisions.

steps.name: Measure sun hours on berry beds after pruning

activities.name: January: Advance the March & Order 2027 Seed
activities.description: Advance every section one row down the rotation table. Order the resistant-variety input list for the season.

steps.name: Advance rotation march one row; pin to shed
BLS-screened pepper seed (Antebellum/Green Machine/Ninja S10; Emerald Fire/El Jefe)
DMR basil seed (Devotion/Obsession/Prospera Compact)
Intermediate-day onion transplants (Candy/Red Candy Apple/Superstar) for Feb-Mar delivery
Tomato seed (resistant cultivars); 8x 5-gal + 2-4x 20-gal fabric pots

activities.name: Harvest & Clear Spinach off Onion Half [SKIPPED]
activities.description: SKIPPED: garlic and onions now interplant in alternating rows. No spinach to clear.

activities.name: Seed Peppers Indoors (pot annex)
activities.description: Standing backbone. 8-10 weeks before last frost, media 75-80F on a heat mat, 7-14 days to germinate. BLS-resistant bells + jalapenos.

steps.name: Set up heat mat at 75-80F
Pot up as they grow; transplant to 5-gal pots early-mid May (soil temp, not frost)

activities.name: Seed Tomatoes Indoors
activities.description: Standing backbone. Start ~6 weeks before the Apr 25-May 5 transplant date. 6 plants for the single Solanaceae section.

activities.name: Spring Greens into Solanaceae Section
activities.description: Standing backbone. Radish/spinach/leaf lettuce Feb 20 - Apr 10, out before the tomato transplant date.

activities.name: Onion Transplants into Allium Section
activities.description: Standing backbone. Intermediate-day onions into rows 2 & 4, between established garlic. 4 in in-row, 10 in between rows = 2 rows x 36 = 72 bulbs across the full 12 ft section.

activities.name: Filler B Out - Spring Carrots/Beets/Chard into Roots
activities.description: Standing backbone. Clear the mustard greens/mache filler; sow spring carrots, beets, chard Mar 1. Harvest June.

activities.name: Tomato Transplants into Solanaceae
activities.description: Standing backbone. 6 tomatoes, single row at 24 in, staked. Drip only, mulch 2-3 in, strip lower 12 in of foliage.

steps.name: Mulch 2-3 in and set drip line (never overhead)

activities.name: Filler A Out - Squash/Cucumber into Cucurbits
activities.description: Standing backbone. Clear filler; sow squash/cucumber May 5-15. Prefer C. moschata (Tromboncino) for vine-borer resistance; trellis on north edge.

activities.name: Peppers & Basil into Pots / Patio
activities.description: Standing backbone. Peppers into 5-gal pots early-mid May for soil temperature, not frost. DMR basil at the patio.

activities.name: Harvest Garlic then Onions
activities.description: Mid-late Jun. Pull garlic first (watch for scapes as the signal), then onions 2-3 weeks later. With alternating rows, loosen garlic from the bed edge with a fork to avoid disturbing adjacent onion rows. Strawberries renovate after yr 1-2 harvest, pull only after yr 3.

steps.name: Cure garlic and onions

activities.name: Jul 1 Handoffs - Peas, Buckwheat, Fall Tomatoes
activities.description: Standing backbone. Southern peas behind the pulled strawberries; buckwheat over Roots and Alliums; fall determinate tomatoes into pots.

activities.name: Seed Fall Brassicas Indoors
activities.description: Standing backbone. THE habit that unlocks the system - seed cabbage + collards Jul 2-24 while it's 95F. Miss it and there's no fall crop. Grow your own starts (clubroot).

steps.name: Set a phone alarm - broadcast reminder

activities.name: Order Strawberry Plugs
activities.description: Order certified plugs for the Sep 20 set. Next planting goes to the section vacating Alliums (N1 in 2029). Only every 3rd year in the 5+1 rotation.

activities.name: Mow Allium Buckwheat at Flowering
activities.description: Standing backbone. Mow at flowering to prevent reseeding.

activities.name: Fall Brassica Transplants Out
activities.description: Standing backbone. Set the home-grown fall brassica starts Aug 13-28 after hardening off.

steps.name: Harden off 5-7 days before transplant

activities.name: Sow Mustard Greens & Mache (Filler B) into Cucurbits
activities.description: Sep 1 -- sow mustard greens + mache into the Cucurbits section as Filler B (117 d, Gap B). Pull mustard by late Feb; must clear by Mar 1 for incoming Roots. Mustard is Brassicaceae, 6+ yr to next brassica on this section -- very safe.

activities.name: Strawberry Plugs In
activities.description: Set certified plugs Sep 20 into N1 (the section Alliums just vacated). 3-year stay with annual renovation. Next planting year after this: 2032.

activities.name: Relay-Seed Mache & Spinach (Filler A) under Standing Tomatoes
activities.description: Oct 1-10 -- broadcast mache + spinach while tomatoes are still in. By Nov 5 pull the filler has 4 weeks on it. Must clear by May 5 for Cucurbits. Spinach is Chenopodiaceae, 2.5 yr to next chenopod on this section -- safe.

activities.name: Garlic In (standing) - Oct 15
activities.description: Standing backbone. Certified seed garlic into rows 1 & 3 of the Allium section, Oct 15 - Nov 10. Full 12 ft, interplanted with onions (rows 2 & 4 go in Feb). Straw mulch garlic rows in November.

steps.name: Straw-mulch the garlic in November

activities.name: Pot Up Olive Tree
activities.description: Establish the olive in its container at the pot annex. Cold-hardy cultivar (Arbequina or Arbosana) in a large pot (15+ gal) with fast-draining gritty mix -- olives rot in wet feet. Full sun spot. If the tree is already potted, just complete this.

steps.name: Source cold-hardy olive (Arbequina/Arbosana) if not already bought
Get 15+ gal pot and fast-draining mix
Water in and confirm drainage

activities.name: Move Olive Indoors for Winter
activities.description: Potted olive roots are damaged well before the top is -- shelter before hard frost. Bright, cool, unheated-ish spot (garage window, sunroom): olives want a cool winter, not living-room heat. Water sparingly all winter.

steps.name: Clear the overwintering spot and check it gets light
Check for pests before bringing indoors

activities.name: Move Olive Back Outside
activities.description: Back to full sun at the pot annex once frost risk has passed (avg last frost ~Apr 12-15). Harden off gradually -- shade first, then sun -- so winter foliage doesn't scorch.

steps.name: Start hardening off (a few hours outside daily)
Prune to shape and feed half-strength balanced fertilizer

activities.name: Strawberry Renovation (Year 1)
activities.description: Mow foliage 1 week post-harvest, thin runners to 4-6 in spacing, side-dress with balanced fertilizer. Do NOT pull — strawberries stay 3 years.

steps.name: Mow foliage to 3-4 in, 1 week after last harvest
Thin runners to 4-6 in spacing
Side-dress with 10-10-10 or equivalent

activities.name: Strawberry Renovation (Year 2)
activities.description: Second annual renovation. Same process: mow, thin, side-dress. Pull happens after year 3 harvest (Jun 2029).

steps.name: Mow foliage to 3-4 in, 1 week after last harvest
Thin runners to 4-6 in spacing
Side-dress with 10-10-10 or equivalent

activities.name: Strawberry Final Pull (Year 3)
activities.description: Pull the 3-year-old planting after harvest. Section goes to Legumes (peas Jul 1). Next strawberry planting: N1 in Sep 2029.

steps.name: Clear all plant material and plastic mulch (if used)
Amend and prep for southern peas Jul 1

activities.name: Sow Gap C Filler (Mache & Arugula) in S2
activities.description: S2 finishes Alliums Sep 1, 2027 and transitions to Leg→Brass Jul 1, 2028 (Gap C, 303 d). Sow mache + arugula as winter greens. Clear by late Jun 2028.

steps.name: Harvest baby greens through winter
Clear all filler by Jun 15 for incoming Legumes Jul 1

activities.name: Sow Spinach + Romaine in S3 (Gap Filler)
activities.description: Direct-sow spinach (Bloomsdale Long Standing) and romaine lettuce in S3 after tomato pull. Cool-season gap filler to hold bed through winter. Spinach: 1-inch spacing broadcast, thin to 4-inch. Romaine: 8-inch spacing in rows. Both frost-tolerant, will produce through fall and overwinter under row cover.

steps.name: Thin spinach to 4-inch spacing at 2 inches tall
Apply row cover at first frost threat

activities.name: Clear Spinach + Romaine from S3
activities.description: Pull remaining spinach and romaine from S3 to prepare bed for Year 2027 tomato transplants. Compost residue, amend soil, let bed rest 2 weeks before transplanting.
